findings.message: The change edits the locked acceptance tests so they skip the menu-action path the change rewired, so the tests no longer check that Pull and Push, as the user triggers them, finish and update the project. acceptance.md says "The baseline's tests are the locked acceptance tests". Yet the diff replaces `leftPlugin.pull!!.run()` / `push!!.run()` (the Runnable registered via addMenuAction) with `leftPlugin.plugin.pull()` / `push()`, and widens `pull`/`push` from `private` to `internal` in Plugin.kt (lines 540, 578) so they can be called. Under the new wiring (`addMenuAction("Pull") { kotlin.concurrent.thread { this.pull() } }`), the original `pull!!.run()` would return as soon as it started the thread, and the assertions would race the worker. The test was moved to match the implementation rather than the behaviour. No recorded reason or approver appears in the packet.

Nothing stops two Pull/Push operations from running at once, so a double key press, or a Push while a Pull's conflict dialog is open, runs two workers against the same repository files and loses or corrupts sync state. Each menu action and key binding (lines 44-54) starts a new `kotlin.concurrent.thread { this.pull() }` / `push()` with no lock, flag or single-thread executor. Before the change, `guiContext.uiRun(this::pull)` serialised them on the EDT. Each worker does readLocalRepository → projectToLocalRepository → readRemoteRepository → writeLocalRepository/writeRemoteRepository on the same `${options.repository}` and `.local` files (`File(...).writer()` truncates on open). For example: press ctrl+\ twice, or press ctrl+shift+\ while `dialogConflictResolver` blocks the first worker in `invokeAndWait`. The two threads interleave reads and writes, and one overwrites the other's merged version vectors, or one reads a half-written file and hits the "corrupt. Requires manual fixing" path.

The worker thread reads the project's renames and comments off the EDT and applies the merged result later through an asynchronous invokeLater, so any rename the user makes in between is silently overwritten and dropped from the local repository. `projectToLocalRepository` (called at lines 550 and 589) reads `context!!.args.codeData.renames/comments` on the background thread while the GUI can still change them. The merged state is written to disk (`writeLocalRepository`) and only afterwards applied in `uiRun { localRepositoryToProject(localRepository) ... }` (lines 572-575, 645-648). `localRepositoryToProject` calls `setProjectRenames(newProjectRenames)`, which replaces the whole list. A rename made while the pre-pull script runs, or while the conflict dialog is open, is therefore lost from the project and was never recorded in the `.local` file. Unsynchronised cross-thread access to the JadxCodeData lists is also a data race.

An unexpected exception in the new worker thread may end the Pull/Push silently, with no dialog, leaving the user unsure whether sync happened. `kotlin.concurrent.thread { this.pull() }` installs no try/catch and no uncaught-exception handler. Code reached from pull/push can throw: `context!!`, `localRepository!!`, `oldLocalRepositoryItem!!`, `newProjectItem!!`, `ProcessBuilder(command).start()` in `runScript` (throws IOException for a bad script path) and `process.waitFor()`. Before the change, these ran inside guiContext.uiRun on the EDT, where the host application's EDT exception handling applied. Now they go to the default thread handler, which only logs to stderr.

No test covers the threading the change introduces (background execution, EDT marshalling of the conflict dialog, async application of results), so a regression in any of it would pass the suite. The mock runs `uiRun` synchronously (`doAnswer { it.getArgument<Runnable>(0).run() }`). The tests call `plugin.pull()`/`push()` directly on the test thread, and each test passes its own conflictResolver lambda, so `dialogConflictResolver`'s `isEventDispatchThread`/`invokeAndWait` branches and the `InterruptedException`/`InvocationTargetException` handling are never run. Nothing exercises the `kotlin.concurrent.thread` wiring at lines 44-54 of Plugin.kt.

The new code uses fully-qualified names where the file and its neighbours use imports, and adds a second logger, which is inconsistent and harder to read. ConflictResolvers.kt already has `import javax.swing.*` yet writes `javax.swing.SwingUtilities.isEventDispatchThread()` and `javax.swing.SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait`. Plugin.kt writes `javax.swing.SwingUtilities.invokeLater` and `kotlin.concurrent.thread` inline. ConflictResolvers.kt adds a file-private `LOG = KotlinLogging.logger {}` even though `Plugin.LOG` (logger ID `jadx-collaboration`) exists, so conflict-dialog errors log under a different logger name than the rest of the plugin.

Renames and comments edited while a sync runs are silently overwritten when it completes. Start Pull with a slow pre-pull script, then edit a rename or comment in the responsive GUI. pull() captures project data in projectToLocalRepository() before running the script, then localRepositoryToProject() replaces the complete project rename and comment lists with that earlier snapshot plus remote changes. It never reconciles edits made during the script. push() has the same snapshot-and-replace sequence.

Repeated sync actions run concurrently against the same repository files, allowing stale results to overwrite newer changes. Every menu and keyboard invocation creates an independent thread without an in-flight guard or serialization. Trigger Pull while Push is waiting in its post-push script: both can read the same .local baseline, independently merge, and later overwrite .local and project state in completion order. writeRepository() also opens the shared destination directly with writer(), without locking or atomic replacement, so overlapping writes can corrupt the JSON.

The modified tests bypass the asynchronous entry points and leave the new threading behavior untested. RepositoryMockery now invokes plugin.pull() and plugin.push() directly instead of the registered menu callbacks. PluginMockery executes uiRun callbacks inline, and the diff adds no tests for worker execution, EDT dispatch, overlapping operations, or edits during synchronization; the existing assertions therefore cannot detect the concurrency regressions introduced here.
